programs.desc: MSM's Life Empowerment services provide participants with tools and support to avoid homelessness, achieve stability, and move toward self-sustainability through various services: financial management and life-skills education, short-term financial assistance, one-on-one coaching, and personalized community resource referrals. Our core program is a 5-month workshop that guides participants in establishing long-term goals and developing relationships and resources to support long-term sustainability.

MSM's Identification Assistance services provide comprehensive support for obtaining Texas identification cards, birth certificates, and driver's licenses - essential documents for accessing employment, housing, banking, and other life-stabilizing resources. This 30+-year-old, volunteer-fueled program is Houston's primary ID assistance provider, receiving over 70 community agency referrals. programs.desc: Women, Work, and Calling- This program is an ecosystem of individuals and organizations committed to equipping Christian women for godly influence in public life. It consists of a large annual event with a local and international audience, quarterly professional development webinars and networking events, 5-month leadership intensives, and various small group learning opportunities.

Public events - The Denver Institute hosts public events in partnership with churches, businesses, and nonprofits on topics related to theology, work, calling, culture, and a wide array of professional industries.

Educational resources - This program includes over 27 courses on Denver Institute's Faith and Work Classroom platform, hundreds of blog posts, multiple books, and episodes of two regularly released podcasts. The program also includes training and speaking engagements at churches, businesses, and other organizations. Through these avenues, the Denver Institute equips participants with resources to develop their vocational discipleship, deepen connections with others, and change their workplaces and cities.

CityGate - This initiative connects leaders and organizations similar to The Denver Institute from across the country who are committed to a Christian vision for their cities. CityGate hosts annual gatherings, regular training webinars, and supports the development of vocational discipleship programs like the 5280 Fellowship in other cities. Supported by a significant multi-year grant, CityGate also produces and distributes a nationwide library of stories and resources designed to inspire faithfulness, vocational imagination, and cultural renewal through work.

592814255.mission: THE PURPOSE OF THE ORGANIZATION IS TO TRANSFORM THE LIVES OF HOMELESS MEN, WOMEN, AND CHILDREN BY PROVIDING CRUCIAL SERVICES TO END THEIR CRISIS OF HOMELESSNESS.

programs.desc: SHELTER SERVICES INCLUDE OUR TWO (2) SHELTER PROGRAMS: THE CENTER FOR WOMEN AND FAMILIES (CWF) AND THE MEN'S SERVICE CENTER (MSC). THE CWF IS A 220-PERSON CAPACITY HOUSING FIRST PROGRAM FOR SINGLE WOMEN AND FAMILIES. THE MSC IS A 240-PERSON CAPACITY HOUSING FIRST PROGRAM FOR SINGLE MEN. COALITION IS A LOW BARRIER SHELTER WITH A FOCUS ON HOUSING, EMERGENCY SERVICES, AND DIVERSION. OUR INTENT IS TO HELP THE HOMELESS RETURN TO STABLE, PERMANENT HOMES AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE. EACH PERSON THAT ENTERS INTO THE SHELTER RECEIVES INDIVIDUALIZED CASE MANAGEMENT THAT BEGINS BY COMPLETING AN INITIAL PERSON-CENTERED ASSESSMENT. THE CASE MANAGER AND THE CLIENT CREATE A "HOUSING FOCUSED" INDIVIDUALIZED CASE PLAN THAT PROVIDES FLEXIBILITY TO MEET THEIR IMMEDIATE AND CRUCIAL NEEDS.

REHOUSING SERVICES INCLUDES RAPID REHOUSING (RRH) AND BRIDGE HOUSING (BH). RAPID REHOUSING IS A SUPPORTIVE HOUSING PROGRAM INTENDED TO PROVIDE PERMANENT HOUSING FOR INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES; CURRENTLY SERVES 53 FAMILIES WITH ROOM FOR GROWTH. RRH IS AN IMPORTANT INTERVENTION TOOL DESIGNED TO QUICKLY CONNECT PEOPLE TO HOUSING AND SERCIVES THROUGH THREE CORE COMPONENTS: HOUSING IDENTIFICATION, RENT AND MOVE IN ASSISTANCE, AND CASE MANAGEMENT. BH PROVIDES A TRANSITIONAL PROGRAM FOR FAMILIES THAT HAVE BEEN APPROVED FOR RRH FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO HELP PAY RENT THAT ARE ALSO ATTACHED TO AN RRH CASE MANAGER; CURRENTLY SERVES EIGHT FAMILIES IN OUR ON-SITE APARTMENTS WITH SPACE.

OTHER EMERGENCY SERVICES PROVIDED BY COALITION INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: DIVERSION - ENGAGE LITERALLY HOMELESS INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES DURING CRISIS TO HELP THEM AVOID ENTERING THE HOMELESS SYSTEM. COMMUNITY HEALTH INITIATIVE (CHI) - OFFERS SHOWERS, LAUNDRY, HYGIENE ITEMS, HEALTH ASSESSMENTS, ACCESS TO A MAILING ADDRESS, FREE CLOTHING AS NEEDED, AND REFERRALS FOR UNSHELTERED HOMELESS, INDIVIDUALS, AND FAMILIES. VICTIMS OF CRIMES ACT (VOCA) PROGRAM - PROVIDES ADVOCACY, REFERRALS, EDUCATION, FINANCIAL RESTITUTION, AND SUPPORT FOR THOSE INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES THAT HAVE BEEN VICTIMS OF CRIMES. VETERANS ADMINISTRATION (VA) CONTRACTED EMERGENCY RESIDENTIAL SERVICES (CERS) - INTENSIVE HOUSING-FOCUSED CASE MANAGEMENT, FREE LAUNDRY, TRANSPORTATION, AND CONNECTION TO EMPLOYMNET AND MAINSTREAM SERVICES FOR VETERANS BASED ON REFERRALS FROM THE VA LIASON.

POLITICS AND PUBLIC OPINION SCHOLARS FOCUS ON POLLING, ELECTIONS, AND POLITICAL THEORY. SOCIETY AND CULTURE SCHOLARS STUDY AND COMMENT ON LIBERAL EDUCATION (SPECIFICALLY, THE HUMANITIES, HIGHER EDUCATION, AND CLASSICAL EDUCATION), CIVIL INSTITUTIONS, THE MEDIA, AMERICAN HISTORY, AND RELIGION.

programs.desc: In 2024, Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Tarrant County (BGCGTC) served 76,398 youth across Tarrant, Dallas, and Denton counties through daily afterschool and summer programs. Club members ages 518 participated in evidence-based activities centered on four core outcomes: Academic Success, Healthy Lifestyles, Good Character & Citizenship, and Workforce Readiness. Mobile Clubhouses expanded access to communities without stand-alone sites, while facility and safety enhancements improved the Club experience. Financial assistance ensures that no youth is denied access to programs due to an inability to pay. Programs provide daily mentorship, academic support, and nutritious meals, creating a safe and positive environment for youth to learn and grow.

BGCGTC emphasizes education and workforce readiness through pre-college programs such as Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search. In 2024, these programs served low-income and first-generation students through tutoring, academic mentoring, college readiness workshops, and career exploration activities. 93% of participants expected to graduate from high school, and 94% reported gaining skills that prepare them for future employment. These programs equip youth to succeed academically, plan for college, and pursue career goals that build long-term economic stability.

The Comin Up Program and related Youth Prevention initiatives served youth ages 1224 through gang-intervention, prevention, and mental-health support services. In 2024, 5,036 youth participated in evidence-based prevention curriculum, 572 positive alternatives reached 10,228 youth and 2,475 adults, and 421 one-time presentations on mental health and substance use education engaged 10,982 youth and 4,187 adults. Counseling services included 98 mental-health assessments and 69 members enrolled in counseling. Programs were delivered by trained social workers and counselors using evidence-based models endorsed by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to build resilience, support families, and reduce risk factors for youth in high-need communities.

BGCGTC expanded its Healthy Lifestyles initiatives through the Blue Door Kitchen,which served 1,500 scratch-made meals each day to youth across 18 Club locations inTarrant and Dallas counties. Approved by the Texas Department of Agriculture as theonly at-risk food provider of its kind in the state, Blue Door Kitchen also launched the Culinary Connection program to teach teens cooking and job-readiness skills. Through these efforts, BGCGTC continues to improve access to healthy food, physical well-being, and community engagement for youth and families.

programs.desc: African Hospitality Institute offers a 2-year immersive English speaking hands-on hospitality vocational program with intensive discipleship training. Students gain experience caring for these visitors who come throughout the year from all over America. 460673585.mission: HTPRC provides support for women facing unplanned pregnancies. We provide free pregnancy tests, clothing, baby formula, diapers, and other supplies. Clients taking computer-assisted classes receive Mommy money to purchase products on Amazon.

programs.desc: The primary program services provided by HTPRC are peer-to-peer counseling of women facing unplanned pregnancies, referrals to other services within the community, including adoption, consumable supplies for the babies (primarily diapers, formula, and baby wipes), baby and maternity clothing, and pregnancy tests for self-administration. We can also refer clients to an OB-GYN for free ultrasound images of the developing babies. Our clients reside in one of the poorest areas of town.

Women who become clients of HTPRC are offered participation in an incentive-driven, computer-based education program that provides training and information regarding their pregnancy from prenatal to post-natal. For completing lessons, the women earn 'mommy money' that they can redeem for necessities for their babies - e.g. strollers, car seats, play pens and cribs. These are items the women often would go without or depend on family or friends for hand-me-downs.

programs.desc: Contributor Program: Young Voices' Contributor Program provides pro bono op-ed editing, pitching, and broadcast interview placement services to talented writers ages 18-35 knowledgeable in the classical liberal tradition. Our last fiscal year we successfully placed 2,153 media hits (e.g. op-ed, radio, TV, podcast, etc.) in noted outlets including Fox News, USA Today, and the Wall Street Journal, reaching an estimated audience of 153 million. Beyond our entry-level placement services, Young Voices also offers continuing education and mentorship services for the top talents in our program, including fellowship programs, summits, professional mentorship, and other PR services for young professionals in our network.

The Dissident Project: The Dissident Project is a speakers bureau founded by Young Voices to educate American high schoolers about the value of liberty through the firsthand stories of people who have lived without it. Since launching in 2022, the Dissident Project has delivered 151 talks to more than 25,000 students nationwide, sharing powerful lessons from immigrants who escaped tyranny for freedom.

Young Voices Europe:Launched in 2022, Young Voices Europe offers article placement services to classical liberal writers living in the European Union. At a time when European political discourse is stuck between the regulatory overreach and speech restrictions of the progressive left and the nationalist and isolationist tendencies of the hard right, Young Voices Europe is introducing the Old World to fresh perspectives promoting consumer choice and individual liberties.

Human Dignity Fellowship:YV aims to amplify the voices of young people pushing back against statism in Europe. Through training and mentorship, YV will showcase young people who are championing freedom in Europe's least free countries. They will write and publish op-eds in the mainstream media in their countries, standing up for property rights, economic freedom, and equality before the law. The result will be a chorus of coordinated but distinct young voices who proclaim the cause of freedom and dignity in the countries where they are most sorely lacking.

204374795.mission: PROVIDE FOOD TO PEOPLE IN NEED, ADVOCATE FOR THE HUNGRY AND EDUCATE THE PUBLIC ABOUT HUNGER ISSUES.

programs.desc: THE MEMBER AGENCY PROGRAM (ALSO KNOWN AS THE FOOD TO NONPROFITS PROGRAM) RELIES ON PARTNERSHIPS WITH HUNDREDS OF NONPROFIT AGENCIES IN THE COMMUNITY THAT HELP THE SAN DIEGO FOOD BANK PROVIDE FOOD ASSISTANCE AND SUPPORT TO HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES WHO FACE FOOD INSECURITY IN THE SAN DIEGO REGION. IN THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED 6/30/25, THE SAN DIEGO FOOD BANK WORKED WITH MORE THAN 450 NONPROFIT PARTNERS THAT INCLUDED FOOD PANTRIES, SOUP KITCHENS, SHELTERS, LOW-INCOME DAYCARE CENTERS, AFTER SCHOOL PROGRAMS, SENIOR CENTERS, AND DISABILITY PROGRAMS TO DISTRIBUTE FOOD AND NONFOOD ITEMS TO PEOPLE IN NEED.

THE EMERGENCY FOOD ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (EFAP, ALSO KNOWN AS TEFAP) IS A FEDERAL PROGRAM THAT PROVIDES MONTHLY EMERGENCY AND SUPPLEMENTAL FOOD TO INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES WHO MEET INCOME GUIDELINES SET BY THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT. IN THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED 6/30/25, THE SAN DIEGO FOOD BANK SERVED AN AVERAGE OF 85,000 INDIVIDUALS PER MONTH THROUGH THE EFAP PROGRAM AND DISTRIBUTED OVER 12 MILLION POUNDS OF FOOD INVENTORY.

THE COMMODITY SUPPLEMENTAL FOOD PROGRAM (CSFP) IS A FEDERALLY SUPPORTED PROGRAM THAT PROVIDES FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION TO SENIORS OVER THE AGE OF 60. THE PROGRAM PROVIDES PARTICIPANTS WITH A 40-POUND BOX OF FOOD EVERY MONTH THAT IS FILLED WITH A VARIETY OF NUTRITIOUS FOOD ITEMS. IN THE FISCAL YEAR ENDED 6/30/25, THE SAN DIEGO FOOD BANK SERVED APPROXIMATELY 15,000 SENIORS EVERY MONTH AND DISTRIBUTED JUST OVER 6 MILLION POUNDS OF FOOD.

THE SAN DIEGO FOOD BANK OPERATES SEVERAL ADDITIONAL PROGRAMS THAT DISTRIBUTE NUTRITIOUS FOOD TO PEOPLE IN NEED, INCLUDING THE FOOD 4 KIDS BACK PACK PROGRAM, FARM TO FAMILY (WHICH DISTRIBUTES FRESH PRODUCE,) AND CALFRESH OUTREACH.

They wanted trained positive adult role models to provide consistent and direct mentoring for students to address unprecedented levels of classroom disruptions, student conflicts and other behavior issues. The program is designed to serve 100 students per grade at partner middle schools through small group and 1:1 mentoring. We continue to serve these students through eighth grade, when possible, while adding a new group of sixth grade students each year. 1:1 Mentoring with Volunteers:In our traditional 1:1 mentoring program we match children and youth (Littles) with caring adult volunteers (Bigs). The program is individualized for each child to meet their social, emotional and academic needs. Parents/guardians enroll their children in our program and work with program staff to identify issues their child may be dealing with, areas of concern and goals for the mentoring relationship. Our staff then create a personalized match plan for each youth outlining specific goals that can be monitored and supported for the duration of the match. Volunteers and youth are matched based on a range of criteria including geographic proximity, personality, life experiences and shared interests. Beyond School Walls workplace mentoring program:In our Beyond School Walls workplace mentoring program, high school students (Littles) are matched with corporate volunteers (Bigs) in 1:1 mentoring relationships. Matches meet as a group for two hours/month at the mentor's workplace and engage in sessions facilitated by BBBSMA staff. The curriculum focuses on career and college readiness, along with relational skill development. Sessions allow a Big and Little to participate in a shared activity while building relationship and conversation. Each year of the curriculum correlates to the next, but is designed so that a Little can enter the program at any year within the cycle. 851300675.mission: To break the cycle of extreme poverty and to offer hope and a future to the most vulnerable children and families living in Korah, Ethiopia.

programs.desc: Family Empowerment: We seek to support families to thrive by providing resources that help them stabilize their health, gain access to educational and vocational training, and foster their relationships within their families and with their community. During 2024, 57 families received monthly rent and groceries, 16 families received beds and mattresses, 246 holiday chickens were distributed, and 350 children and 57 adults received shoes and socks.

Education: Education for all ages is key to breaking the cycle of poverty. HFK supports each family member from the oldest to the youngest. Helping adults gain training tailored to their social history and current abilities, enabling them to become self-sustaining. Providing children with the education and the support needed to increase their chances for a better future. Graduating post-secondary students can help their families break out of poverty and bring sustainable change to Korah. During 2024, 264 students received educational support, 172 students attended after-school tutoring and after-school snacks, 78 students received academic awards, 99 students enrolled in computer /ICT classes, and 16 received vocational training.

Health and Nutrition: Health stability and nutritional support are critical aspects of helping children, families, and elders to overcome the formidable barriers that living in extreme poverty has placed in their lives. We have 5 programs that serve health and nutrition needs. 1) The Berta Breakfast Program: provided 550+ children with fortified pancakes and milk before school. 2) The HFK Daycare: 50 preschool children received 2 daily meals and snacks. 3) Youth Programs: 350 children received regular after-school snacks, and 520 children received regular snacks. 4) The Elders' Home: provided 9 elders with leprosy daily support, including housing, food, sundries, clothing, medical care, and special outings. 5) Health Services programs: provided 1500+ families access to free medical services and prescriptions, 120 families received annual health insurance policies, 8 people received hospi

Economic Empowerment: To spur families towards economic empowerment and independence, HFK facilitates business training, Self-Help Group participation, and social work support to build community connections, provide relevant skills, and empower families to launch their initiatives. In 2024, 15 adults developed business and employment plans, 16 adults received business grants, 80 adults attended business and employment training sessions, 21 adults received life skills training, 7 adults received literacy and numeracy training, 29 adults attended adult continuing education, and 1 additional savings and credit self-help group was created.

programs.desc: Well-Being: HOPE's overarching goal is to enhance the quality of life for the entire post-9/11 Warrior Community. HOPE views well-being, or wellness as positive and affirming; an active process in which people become aware of, and make choices toward, a more prosperous and purposeful life. HOPE's well-being model integrates six well-being domains that were developed to meet the complex needs of the Warrior Community. See Schedule O for continuation

Cohen Veterans Network: The Steven A. Cohen Military Family Clinic at Hope for The Warriors provides confidential, high-quality behavioral health care services at little to no cost without long wait times to post-9/11 veterans, active duty service members with a TRICARE referral, and military families. The Clinic is a local resource connection for the community, including Camp Lejeune, Jacksonville, and the greater Onslow County area. See Schedule O for continuation

Cultural Awareness: HOPE's communications team drives the initiative to bridge the military-civilian divide through understanding of the needs of the veteran community and military families, and how the public at large can support them. The team facilitates dialogue, primarily through digital platforms, that brings awareness of and respect for the existing cultural differences and experiences. Additionally, sustained awareness of the needs of the military community results in effective programming for the DOD, Department of Veteran's Affairs, and socially-responsible corporate entities. This team informs HOPE and its partners with metrics and engagement strategies that continue that connection.

Community Engagement:HOPE works directly at the community level to engage both military and civilian communities, uniting corporate and civil leaders, school districts, military agencies, and more to work together with a shared goal of embracing the military families within their communities. HOPE provides education and resources, both in person and virtually, to service members and their families as they transition out of the military. By developing relationships within the community - through both events and program work - HOPE establishes connectedness to community that is also a key component of the warrior culture.

204718695.mission: The Folk Heritage Associations mission is to provide living history experiences and to preserve the heritage of Macon County for generations to come. Our main projects include the Womens History Trail, WHT Sculpture Project, Macon Matriarch, and other heritage related activitie

programs.desc: FHAMC/WHT Sculputre and Park Project: On March 23, 2024 after 7 years of working toward our goal, FHAMC donated Sowing the Seeds of the Future an historic bronze sculputure, to the Town of Franklin as public art. This sculputure which serves as the trailhead for the WHT Walking Trail depicts three women - Na-Ka Rebeccas Morris (a Cherokee woman) Salley (an enslaved woman) and Harret Tiomozena Siler Sloan (a pioneer woman) that all had a conection to the land near the river where the sculpture is placed. FHAMC helped create a pocket park near the river, The Womens History Park, where the is important sculpture is placed.

The Womens History Trail Walking Trail, Scholarship, Matriarch and other events: The Trail celebrate the livess of local historical women along a self-guided walking trail (currently 20 sites). By providing activities and educational events, we strive to share stories about important women who helped shape Macon Countys history. We continue to recognize living elderly women in the area as a WHT Macon Matriarch each March to acknowledge their accomplishments during Womens History Month. In May, our group gives a scholarship to a high school senior to help prepare for a bright future. Our connection to uplift women in the past, present and future is an important element of the Womens History Trail.

FHAMC Heritage Projects: Throughout this year, FHAMC provides skill demonstrations and hands on activities for students in various settings, i.e. Macon County Fair, 4th Grade Heritage Day, Cowee Christmas, etc. Our focus is not a building but instead we focus on programs and projects to enhance education while giving the community opportunities to participate in heritage related themes. As a co sponser of 4th Grade Heritage Day, our organization works with other like minded groups to provide hertiage activites such as : quiliting, square dancing, pottery, Native American booth, primitive arts, crafts, music etc. in order to give students hands-on activities that highlight the heritage of our area. Our board members are volunteers also host demonstrations at Cowee Christmas.

201234015.mission: THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF GEORGIA MUSEUMS, INC. IS THE OPERATION OF FOUR MUSEUMS: BARTOW HISTORY MUSEUM, BOOTH WESTERN ART MUSEUM, TELLUS SCIENCE MUSEUM AND SAVOY AUTOMOBILE MUSEUM.

programs.desc: Booth Western Art Museum is a 120,000 square-foot museum with galleries of western contemporary art. Additional galleries feature Presidential letters and photographs, American West art, and fine art photography. In addition to the permanent galleries, there are four galleries with temporary exhibits. Booth offers evening lectures, art for lunch programs, and art classes at the nearby Booth Art Academy regularly during the year. The museum also has a nearby satellite gallery that sells artwork from local artists, as well as prints, posters, and books. During fiscal year 2025, 35,886 individuals visited the museum. During the school year 2024-2025, 16,639 students participated in an educational program or experience. The Booth Western Art Museum has 1,572 active members.

Tellus Science Museum, a 120,000 square-foot museum dedicated to science, has a mineral gallery, fossil gallery, interactive children's science gallery, transportation gallery, gem panning area, and a fossil dig area. Within the museum there are three temporary exhibit galleries hosting changing exhibits during the year. In addition, there is a digital planetarium with shows throughout the day. Visitors can also visit the solar house and other outdoor exhibits. In fiscal year 2025, Tellus had 150,003 visitors, including 15,828 people seeing a planetarium show. During the school year 2024-2025, 43,474 students participated in student educational programs. Tellus Science Museum has 3,606 active members.

Savoy Automobile Museum celebrates automobiles throughout the 66,000 square foot museum with one permanent gallery as well as three temporary galleries with changing exhibits such as women in motorsports, 75 Years of Porsche, etc. The museum hosted one local car show this past year. There is a beautiful artwork collection that celebrates automobiles located throughout the facility. An additional 34,000 square-foot storage building on the campus houses permanent collection vehicles when not on exhibit. During the fiscal year 2025, 66,718 individuals visited the museum. Savoy Museum has 3,112 active members.

Talent Search Counselors also assist students with the shift from high school to college, through their first semester in college.
